compositor.support/support.smithay/smith.reason: The neutral Wire's one seam to the world side: it grows a method per world capability the smithay handlers need (space, focus, pointer warp, surface-to-world mapping), and splitting the trait would split a single contract across crates.

compositor.installer/installer.process/p.reason: Per-distro package enumeration list; inherently a flat list, splitting adds no value.
Per-distro package enumeration list; inherently a flat list, splitting adds no value.

compositor.expansion/compositor.backgrou.reason: The System impl carries the full per-world background lifecycle in one module: register + update (resolve shader / rebuild GPU resource / gate on lock) + draw + the buffer command handler + camera event handlers. The storage tokens and persistence Document now live in two.storage; this is the remaining system logic, which reads as one unit.

The worker handle and its three channels are one unit: the draw signal in, the pane registry out, and the readback out. Splitting the handle from the channels it owns would make them reachable without it, which is exactly the global this feature spent its life removing. The bulk is why each channel exists and which thread writes it.

compositor.expansion/compositor.pipeline.reason: An ABI definition and the one function that writes it. The bulk is the rationale for each lane and each flag, which is the whole value of the file: every shipped bundle restates this layout in WGSL and none of them can be recompiled from here, so what a lane means has to be written down beside it. Splitting the flags from the packer would put a constant and its only writer in different crates.

The seam builder and the pointer warp that answers against the same pipeline. They are one unit: `multipass_pass` pushes each pass from the live param array and `warp_point` must resolve the warp from that same array, so splitting them puts the picture and the cursor correction in different crates with nothing holding them to the same values.

Mostly an asset table: one line per shipped bundle file, plus the path normalisation that lets bundles share sources across folders. Splitting the data from the four accessors that read it would put the two halves in different crates for no reader's benefit.

The per-world slot, its tokens and the system that maintains it are one unit: `y5_storage!` makes the write token crate-private on purpose, so splitting the state from its only writer would force that token public and lose the guarantee that nothing else can mutate a world's pipeline tables. The bulk is the rationale for the liveness rule, which is the part that is not derivable from the code.

compositor.expansion/compositor.remote/r.reason: Four handler bodies that must stay together: they are the one place the world's background slot is written from outside the settings panel, and the rationale for the three-field write (selection, instance, mark) is what stops the next handler doing two of the three.

The `define!` invocation: one block declaring every gRPC service, its methods and their request/response types. It is a table, and its length is the number of RPCs the compositor exposes. Splitting it would mean two macro invocations building two master enums, which is exactly the thing the single invocation exists to prevent.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.ca.reason: Pass-1 input is whole-handler (Consume is all-or-nothing): CameraSystem::input bundles the over-window hit-test, grab check, and cursor-anchored zoom as one unit; zoom must run on the camera OWNER (synchronous accumulation), so it lives here.

Pass-1 input is whole-handler (Consume is all-or-nothing): CanvasSystem::input bundles the release handler's grab transition + synchronous seat button + iced/resize fan-out as one indivisible unit; splitting it across modules would break the single Consume decision.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.pl.reason: Full-fidelity launch persistence: the serde record types plus the codec-driven hint/preference projection + reconstruction form one cohesive conversion unit.

Owns the placeholder slot and the cross-system geometry channel: an interactive placeholder move/scale must update both this slot (modify_visible) and the iced registry (surface system), so the channel receiver + buffer + the two announce paths live together as one routing unit.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.su.reason: Owns the surface slot + the registry-routing channels (ICED_BUTTON, ICED_FOCUS, ICED_CONTEXT): each is an indivisible announce-fn + channel + buffer-apply triple that input systems use to reach the registry (the only mutation path); they belong on the one slot owner and can't be split without scattering the registry's single write authority.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.vi.reason: Full-fidelity viewport-tree persistence: the serde record types plus the recursive live<->persisted projection form one cohesive conversion unit.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.wi.reason: One record and the single function that observes every edge on it. The alternative to its length is seven lifecycle hooks in six files, which is what this exists to avoid — and the per-moment rationale is what stops the next one being added as an eighth hook somewhere else.

Three near-identical booleans about one window, whose whole difficulty is which consumer reads which — frame callbacks, fractional scale, xdg suspended. The length is the note saying so; without it the next consumer picks whichever name reads best and is wrong in a way nothing catches.

compositor.introspection/introspection.e.reason: The type-erased codec registry (register/encode/decode/make_hint_item/type lookups) is one cohesive unit; splitting the fn-pointer table across crates would obscure it.

compositor.kernel/kernel.execution/execu.reason: One cohesive startup-wiring unit: block_sigchld + install + base_env + the signalfd reaper source share the SIGCHLD-blocked precondition and the single calloop LoopHandle, so they stay together rather than fragmenting the loader wiring.

compositor.kernel/kernel.vulkan/vulkan.c.reason: One composition recording: the damaged and full-redraw variants differ only in the target acquire and the attachment load-op, so they share the barrier + pass choreography rather than duplicating it across two crates.

compositor.orchestration/orchestration.s.reason: A published slot plus the layout of the block it fills. The bulk is why each value is where it is — a lane meaning that lives away from the lane is how a shader and an engine come to disagree about what they are exchanging.

Un-warping a pointer is one function with three conditions on it: whether a warp applies at all, which of the two grid producers answered for this world, and undoing the chain in reverse of how the picture was built. The bulk is that reasoning; a cursor that renders away from where it clicks is the cost of getting any of it wrong.

compositor.orchestration/orchestration.w.reason: WorldManager is one cohesive owner of the world set + active/spawn-target/generation invariants.

compositor.support/support.smithay/smith.reason: Dispatch is the concrete wayland protocol-state aggregate plus its required SeatHandler impl (document/SMITHAY_DECOUPLING.md P2 flip); intentionally large.
31 orphan-rule-bound smithay handler/Dispatch impls must live in the crate defining Wire<S>; helper code already extracted to wire.color/wire.colorsurf/wire.redraw (floor ~397 LOC)
Hand-rolled wlr-foreign-toplevel-management state: mirror + emit + reconcile in one module.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.ov.reason: Per-frame reconciler for the grid's hover card: gate, cursor hit-test, placement and surface lifecycle in one pass; the content halves are already split out to draw.label (title) and draw.icon (the icon fallback chain).
The overlay's rim entry points (toggle / close / logout / deferred-action pump) are one small state machine; each is a handful of lines and splitting them scatters the flag they share.

compositor.extension/compositor.monitor/.reason: One iced view: the hover card bubble plus its icon widget. A view is not divisible below itself.

compositor.introspection/introspection.e.reason: Flat list of zero-sized identity attribute markers; each is a 7-line impl and the list is the module.
The four identity/env/desktop-entry/toplevel-icon hint pushes belong together: their ORDER is the precedence rule (desktop entry over toplevel icon).
Wayland-side Meta capture: the full (surface + credentials + /proc tree) form and the surface-only form share their whole body.

compositor.introspection/introspection.s.reason: The sampler thread's single loop — cadence, forced refresh, batching and flush deadlines are one interleaved state machine.
Queue entries, cadence constants and the registration/refresh application: the timing policy is one document.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.wi.reason: The LoopWindow extension trait plus its single impl for smithay's Window: trait and impl cannot be split apart.

compositor.introspection/introspection.e.reason: Pure façade — the re-export map for the whole extraction subsystem; its length IS the module tree it fronts.
The handler registry (register/detect/extract) plus the two free extraction entry points it exists to expose.
One function: every base hint a process tree yields, in the order their precedence depends on.
Flat list of hint value types; each is a small struct/enum and the list is the module.
Reading the toplevel icon is buffer selection + shm decode + un-premultiply; splitting the format handling from its only caller hides the invariants it checks.

compositor.expansion/compositor.y5/y5.ov.reason: One ordered fallback chain for the hover card's icon. Its length IS the order, and the order is the behaviour — splitting it hides which source beat which.

compositor.introspection/introspection.e.reason: One cache backs both lookups the runtime can answer (name, running state) because both come from a single `podman ps` call; splitting the non-blocking and blocking entry points into separate crates would duplicate the cache or force a shared-state crate between them.

compositor.introspection/introspection.l.reason: The graph itself now lives on the attribute descriptors; what remains is the optional re-derivation layer, where each arm exists BECAUSE of what one specific extractor does. Splitting an arm from the pass that dispatches it would separate a capability from its only caller.

compositor.support/support.smithay/smith.reason: One clipboard transfer, both directions. Handing the worker the capture pipes, admitting what it finished and writing flavors back to a pasting client share the generation bookkeeping and the same non-blocking pipe discipline; splitting them would separate the invariant (only our end is non-blocking, only the client writes) from the code that depends on it.

One protocol: both interfaces of xdg-toplevel-drag-v1 plus the source->drag registry their invalid_source/toplevel_attached/ongoing_drag errors are defined against. The manager exists only to mint the drag object, so splitting them would separate a two-request protocol from the single map that makes its errors decidable.

One slot: the head's flavors, the generation that invalidates them, and the budget arithmetic deciding what may enter. The headroom a reader is granted is a function of what is already admitted plus what the other live readers hold, so moving the budget away from the flavors it bounds would separate the limit from the state it is computed over.

One policy: every limit the clipboard transfer layer answers to — how much is held, for how long in each direction, in what order flavors are taken, and how big a bite each direction takes. They are chosen against each other (the chunk sizes are what the idle windows grant time for; the capture pipe is sized to the read chunk), so splitting them would scatter one set of trade-offs across crates.

One thread and the handle that speaks to it. The command set, the tick that services it and the budget/deadline arithmetic are the same ownership story — fds move in, finished flavors move out, nothing is shared — and splitting the handle from the loop would put the two halves of that protocol in different crates.

One grab: PointerGrab has fourteen methods and this type exists to forward all of them to the wrapped DnDGrab unchanged, adding the carry only in motion. The bulk is the forwarding surface itself, which cannot be split without splitting a single trait impl.

One correlation unit: the claim registry plus both predicates it resolves on (activation token from /proc environ, pid parent chain) — splitting them would separate a lookup from the two ways it answers.

One store: the durable name index plus the live grant bookkeeping the protocol's name_in_use/already_added errors are defined against. Splitting them would separate a lookup from the invariants that make it correct.

compositor.introspection/introspection.l.reason: LaunchPlan's descriptor-keyed accessors (has_pref_override / clear_pref_override / is_pref_enabled) resolve preferences AND inferred hints together — is_pref_enabled defaults from whether a hint exists — so they need both private halves of the plan and cannot be split out.

One type, one private map. The name-keyed accessors the settings UI needs (is_enabled_by_name_or / has_override_by_name / clear_override_by_name) must be methods on Preferences because they read and mutate its private `fields`; hoisting them into a sibling crate would force the map public and make the override/enabled invariants unenforceable.

compositor.kernel/kernel.vulkan/vulkan.f.reason: fourcc -> capability classification table; one flat mapping that every format gate reads, splitting it would separate entries from the rule that reads them.

compositor.kernel/kernel.graphic/graphic.reason: The modifier classification, ranking and the single empty-result vocabulary. Splitting the rules from the words for their outcomes is how four call sites came to answer 'empty' four different ways.
One slot per capability role plus the session facts every answer reads; splitting them would let a reader think a role could be published without the others noticing.
The single fourcc vocabulary. It replaces four disjoint lists that had to be hand-kept in lockstep; splitting it recreates exactly that problem.
THE intersection engine. It absorbs five call sites that disagreed on empty-set policy, INVALID and LINEAR; the point is that all of it is readable in one sitting.
One exhaustive match from consumer to formats, with no wildcard arm. Splitting the arms across crates would defeat the reason it is one function.
Latched reporting for what the negotiation decided and what it cost; the loss report and the allocation report share the de-duplication table.
Raw-ash per-modifier probe of a wgpu adapter: the two-pass enumerate, the usability probe and the adapter pick are one device conversation and read as one.

compositor.support/support.system/system.reason: Thread-safe sibling of Storage: insert/contains/with/with_mut/entry are one addressing scheme and splitting them would separate the lock from what it guards.
